learningObjectives: Place Test Data Service (TDS) within Tricentis' broader Test Data Management (TDM) offering.
Explain the difference between the static, reusable data used in TestCase Design and the consumable, stateful data managed by TDS.
Identify the two main challenges testers face when acquiring and tracking test data.
Explain why 'keeping data stateful' matters for distributed, multi-step, or multi-day testing.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Where TDS fits in Tricentis Test Data Management

elements.description: The umbrella term for Tricentis' holistic data solution, made up of several components: Test Data Service, TDM Studio, qTest, and Flood.

elements.title: The two components most relevant to testers
items: Test Data Service (TDS) — focuses on the test data life cycle; the central hub for storing, retrieving, and updating test records. This course covers TDS exclusively.
TDM Studio — handles data generation, masking production data, and creating synthetic data (not covered in this course).

elements.text: qTest and Flood are separate Tricentis products with their own dedicated training — outside the scope of TDS2.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: TestCase Design vs. Test Data Service

elements.description: TestCase Design structures TestCases to cover every variant and pathway of the SUT, producing the combinations needed for comprehensive coverage. Static data values can be added, but this data is non-consumable — it can be reused multiple times and simultaneously by different TestCases.

TDS acts as a data repository where records can be stored, retrieved, updated, and have their status viewed by multiple people. Unlike TestCase Design's static data, TDS stores consumable/dynamic data that regularly changes — this data can generally only be used once, by one machine, at a time.
Any information fed into the application under test — usernames, passwords, credit card numbers, customer details, reference data, and more.

bulletPoints: TestCase Design's data = static, reusable, simultaneous use. TDS's data = dynamic, consumable, single use at a time.
TDS1 answered 'what data combinations do I need?'. TDS2 answers 'where does that data live, and how do I keep it accurate as tests consume it?'.

elements.description: Complex database structures often require specific data that isn't available in the SUT or is hard to access. A direct SQL query would normally retrieve it, but suitable SQL statements are often missing, or slow and difficult to write. Existing data (production data, or data created in an earlier test) is another option, but retrieving it manually is time-consuming. TDS solves this either way: it can generate the needed test data on demand, or store and adjust already-available data — both with fast response and run times.

elements.term: Challenge 2 — Tracking the state of test data
elements.description: An earlier test frequently changes the data it touched. If inaccurate, old, or already-consumed data gets reused by another TestCase, results become unreliable — a risk that grows sharply when end-to-end TestCases span several days or run on multiple machines.

Two TestCases logging into the same SAP account to modify personal details can't run at the same time; the second must wait for the first to finish and then use the updated values. A more complex case — creating a bank customer, generating an account number, then processing a payment — needs each dynamic value (customer ID, account number) progressively updated in the TDS repository as it's produced, or a later step (like processing the payment) simply won't have a valid ID to work with.

TDS gives visibility into a multi-tester environment by adjusting each record's Status as it moves through the process, and prevents conflicting use of the same record through lock/unlock features. Data can also be created, retrieved, or updated through API calls, which further increases response time and agility when managing test data.

bulletPoints: Challenge 1 = getting the right data in the first place. Challenge 2 = keeping it trustworthy as tests consume and change it.
Status tracking + lock/unlock are what make TDS safe to use across a distributed, multi-tester team.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing TestCase Design's data with TDS's data
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming the static data added to a TestSheet in TDS1 behaves the same way as data stored in TDS.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TestCase Design data is static and reusable — many TestCases can use it simultaneously. TDS data is dynamic and consumable — generally usable once, by one machine, at a time.

examPitfalls.title: Treating TDM Studio and Test Data Service as the same thing
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming data masking/synthetic data generation (TDM Studio) is part of what this course covers.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: TDM Studio (data generation, masking, synthetic data) is a separate TDM component. TDS2 covers Test Data Service only — the storage/retrieval/update hub for the data life cycle.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which statement correctly distinguishes data used in TestCase Design from data managed by Test Data Service (TDS)?

options.text: TestCase Design data is dynamic and consumable; TDS data is static and reusable.
TestCase Design data is static and reusable by multiple TestCases at once; TDS data is dynamic, consumable, and generally usable once at a time.
There is no meaningful difference between the two.
TDS data can only be used by non-UI TestCases.

practiceQuiz.hint: Think about which kind of data can safely be shared simultaneously, and which can't.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TestCase Design's static data is non-consumable and can be reused by multiple TestCases simultaneously. TDS's data is dynamic/consumable — generally usable only once and by one machine at a time, which is exactly why it needs to be tracked statefully.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A test team needs to generate masked, synthetic versions of production data for testing. Which Tricentis TDM component is designed for that job?
practiceQuiz.hint: One component is about the data life cycle (storage/retrieval); another is about generating/masking data itself.
practiceQuiz.rationale: TDM Studio handles the generation of data, masking of production data, and creation of synthetic data. TDS focuses on the test data life cycle (storing, retrieving, updating) rather than generating/masking data itself.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What are the two main challenges testers face when using test data for automation, according to this course's introduction?

options.text: Writing TestCases and executing them on time.
Acquiring specific test data, and ensuring the state of that data is efficiently tracked.
Installing Tosca Server and configuring the network.

practiceQuiz.hint: One challenge is about getting the data; the other is about trusting it stays accurate as it's used.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The two challenges are acquiring specific test data (often blocked by missing/hard-to-write SQL, or slow manual retrieval) and tracking the state of that data so consumed/stale records aren't mistakenly reused.

quickRecap.value: Umbrella term; components include Test Data Service, TDM Studio, qTest, Flood.
Static, non-consumable, reusable simultaneously by multiple TestCases.
Dynamic, consumable, generally usable once by one machine at a time.
Acquiring specific test data (missing/slow SQL, or slow manual retrieval of existing data).
Tracking data state so stale/consumed records aren't reused.
Status tracking + lock/unlock, visible to a distributed team, with API access for speed.
